title: Onboarding eval: mixed-script date/currency/transliteration hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing failure hypotheses and a lightweight test plan for model onboarding focused on mixed-script & locale formatting edge cases: (1) intra-string script switching (Latin + CJK + Arabic), (2) date/time formatting normalization across locales, (3) currency symbol placement and rounding behavior, (4) transliteration fidelity for names and technical terms, and (5) fallback behavior for unsupported locales. The goal is to create a small prioritized prompt set and per-prompt pass/fail signals we can run as part of the smoke/regression harness during onboarding.

Context / motivation:
- Recent model candidate (v2.1-experimental) showed nondeterministic behavior for strings that mix Latin and CJK characters when asked to normalize dates: sometimes it left numerals in Western digits, sometimes converted to native numeral glyphs (fullwidth), breaking downstream parsers.
- We observed three customer incidents in last quarter where chat features produced badly translated invoice line items due to currency formatting mismatch (e.g., “$1,234.56” -> “¥1,234.56” with wrong currency conversion semantics).
- Hypothesis: tokenization differences + locale fallback heuristics in the model cause contextual ambiguity when multiple locale signals are present in prompt (explicit locale tag vs. implicit script).

Quick observational notes (from manual triage):
- Mixed-script names ("Alex 李") => model sometimes returns pinyin for the surname without diacritics, sometimes returns Chinese characters.
- Arabic-Indic numerals appear only when explicit Arabic locale requested; otherwise Western digits used even inside Arabic script contexts.
- Date normalization: prompts that ask for ISO-format output are mostly OK, but when asked to produce a human-friendly date in target locale, the model mixes locale conventions (e.g., uses month/day order for en-GB contexts when the prompt has an explicit en-GB tag).

Failure hypotheses (ranked):
1) Tokenization-anchoring mismatch: model priming with an explicit locale tag is not consistently anchored to generation tokens when the prompt contains strong script cues.
2) Training data sparsity: examples with mixed scripts + numeric formatting are underrepresented, so the model falls back to dominant script conventions.
3) Postprocessing heuristics not activated for certain token sequences (e.g., when fullwidth digits are adjacent to Latin punctuation).
4) Ambiguous currency semantics: model confuses currency symbol formatting with currency conversion intent.
5) Transliteration heuristics vary by entity type (person vs technical term) causing inconsistent outputs.

Proposed small eval prompt set (30 prompts total, grouped):
A. Mixed-script normalization (10 prompts) - expected: deterministic normalization to locale-specified conventions. Examples:
  - Prompt: "Normalize for en-US: 'Invoice dated 2026年05月04日 for amount ¥1,234' ->"
    Expected: "Invoice date: 2026-05-04; Amount: ¥1,234"
  - Prompt: "Locale: zh-HK. Convert: 'Meeting 04/05/2026' -> human format"
    Expected: "2026年5月4日" (note: zh-HK convention clarifications in comments)
  - Prompt: "Text: 'Alex 李 paid $1,200 on 5月4日' -> canonicalize name and date for en-US output"
    Expected: "Alex Li paid $1,200 on 2026-05-04"

B. Date / time formatting edgecases (6 prompts)
  - 12-hour vs 24-hour disambiguation with explicit locale tag (en-US vs fr-FR)
  - Relative date resolution with mixed timezone abbreviations (PDT vs CST ambiguous)

C. Currency placement and rounding (6 prompts)
  - Prompt: "Format 1234.5 for fr-FR and en-GB with currency EUR/GBP"
    Expected: "1 234,50 €" and "£1,234.50" respectively
  - Prompt: "Display amounts for ja-JP (Yen) with no cents and correct symbol"

D. Transliteration and name handling (4 prompts)
  - Prompt: "Transliterate: 'Мария Иванова' into Japanese kana"
    Expectation: consistent transliteration and indication of uncertainty if ambiguous
  - Prompt: "Romanize: '李小龍' ->"
    Expectation: "Li Xiaolong" (note canonical forms vs common stage names)

E. Unsupported-locale fallback checks (4 prompts)
  - Prompt: "Locale: xx-XX (unsupported). Provide best-effort formatting for '04/05/2026' and explain assumptions"
    Expectation: system returns ISO and a short note of assumption

Pass/fail rubric (simple automated checks):
- Exact-match on canonicalized ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) when asked for ISO -> pass.
- Regex-based checks for currency placement and decimal separators per-locale -> pass/fail.
- Transliteration: compare against curated small ground-truth table; if model output variant is in whitelist -> pass; else flag for human review.
- Fallback behavior: must include explicit assumption sentence when locale unsupported -> pass.

Measurement plan:
- Baseline run on current champion model (v2.0-stable) and new candidate (v2.1-experimental). Record per-prompt pass rates, and delta.
- Track two metrics: locale-fidelity (percent of prompts that match per-locale formatting rules) and consistency (percent of prompts where repeated sampling yields same normalized output across 5 seeds).
- Alert criteria for blocking onboarding: any absolute drop >5% locale-fidelity vs champion OR consistency <85% on critical prompts (mixed-script date/currency).

Quick harness notes / implementation guidance:
- We will implement each prompt as a unit test in the onboarding harness. Use deterministic sampling (temperature=0) for pass/fail gating, plus a stochastic check (t=0.7, n=5) to measure consistency.
- Tokenization-investigation hook: if a prompt fails, capture model tokenization boundaries for the prompt and the top candidate output for triage. Add to JIRA-AM-987 with tokenization snapshot.
- Add simple post-processors only for evaluation (not production): normalizer scripts for dates/currency to compute reference form for automated checks. Keep postproc off for model pass gating except when prompt explicitly requests postprocessing.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
- Create prompt set as JSONL in repo (Arjun) - target 2026-05-08.
- Add harness unit tests + tokenization hook (Liam) - target 2026-05-11.
- Run baseline vs candidate & produce regression report (Mai) - target 2026-05-13.
- If failures exceed threshold, schedule deep dive with SRE/tokenization team - target 2026-05-15.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we canonicalize all numeric digits to Western digits in the canonical form, or respect native glyphs when prompt requests human-friendly localized text? (affects downstream parsers)
- For transliteration, what whitelist size is reasonable? We need to balance recall vs false positives; suggest starting with 200 high-frequency names across languages.
- Do we require the model to perform semantic currency conversion when currency symbols change, or only formatting? Propose: only formatting by default; conversion must be explicitly requested.

Notes to self / triage log snippets:
- 2026-04-28: seen sample where '04/05/2026' in en-GB context produced '05/04/2026' (day/month swapped) - add explicit day-first test.
- 2026-04-29: candidate model produced '1.234,5 €' for 1234.5 (missing trailing zero) - rounding formatting test added.

References and helpful links:
- Confluence: Multiscript Onboarding Checklist (linked above)
- GitHub: small normalizer scripts in ml-onboarding repo (PR 399)
- Prior incident notes: customer-INC-2026-03 (currency formatting causing downstream CSV parsing failure)

Comments: This doc is intentionally terse and actionable. The prompt bank is a living artifact; keep it minimal for fast automated gating. Add examples that surfaced real customer pain first. When we have a stable pass, expand to include more languages and currency edgecases (cryptocurrency symbols, local micro-units).

End of note.
